n: God answers the prayer of chapter 64: He has been ready to be found all along, even by people who didn’t look for Him, calling “Here I am, here I am.” Paul applies this to Gentiles coming to Christ.

f.w: I am found of them that sought me not

f.g: Literally “Here I am, here I am”—God eagerly offering Himself.

n: All day long God held out His hands to a rebellious people who followed their own ideas. The image is of a parent reaching out with open arms; Jacob uses it in the Book of Mormon.

f.w: I have spread out my hands all the day

n: They provoke God openly—offering sacrifices in sacred gardens and burning incense on brick altars, practices tied to pagan worship and forbidden by the law.

f.g: God’s law required altars of earth or uncut stone (Exodus 20:24-25).

n: They sit among tombs and spend nights in secret places—probably trying to contact the dead—and eat pork and unclean broth, things the law of Moses forbade.

f.g: Likely seeking oracles from the dead.

n: Worst of all, they say, “Keep away—I’m holier than you!” Such smug pride is like smoke in God’s nose—a constant irritation.
It’s all written down before God. He won’t stay silent; He will repay them fully—into their lap, as grain was measured into a fold of one’s robe.

f.g: Pay back into the fold of their garment, like measured grain.

n: He will repay their sins and their ancestors’ sins, who burned incense on hilltops and insulted Him there.
But not everyone will be destroyed. Just as people say “Don’t destroy that grape cluster—there’s still good juice in it,” God will spare His faithful servants.

f.w: Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it
f.g: Possibly the opening words of a vintage song.

n: He will bring out descendants from Jacob and heirs from Judah to inherit His mountains; His chosen ones will live there.
From the Plain of Sharon in the west to the Valley of Achor in the east, the land will be peaceful pasture for those who seek the Lord. Achor, once a place of judgment, becomes a place of hope.

f.g: The fertile coastal plain of Israel.
“Valley of Trouble,” near Jericho, where Achan was judged (Joshua 7:24-26).

n: But those who abandon the Lord and set tables for Gad and Meni—gods of “Fortune” and “Destiny”—are another story.

f.g: Hebrew Gad—a god of good luck.
Hebrew Meni—a god of fate or destiny.

n: So God will “destine” them for the sword (a wordplay on Meni). When He called, they didn’t answer; they chose what He hated.

f.w: when I called, ye did not answer

n: Contrast: God’s servants will eat, drink, and rejoice, while the rebellious go hungry, thirsty, and ashamed.
His servants will sing from glad hearts; the rebels will cry from broken hearts and wail in anguish.
Their name will become a curse word among God’s chosen, but He will give His servants a different name—a new identity.

f.w: call his servants by another name

n: Anyone who blesses or takes an oath will do it by “the God of truth”—literally “the God of Amen,” whose word is sure—because past troubles are forgotten.

f.g: Hebrew “God of Amen”—the God who is faithful and reliable.

n: God announces: “I create new heavens and a new earth,” and the former troubles won’t even come to mind. Latter-day Saints understand the earth will be renewed in the Millennium and ultimately glorified.

f.w: I create new heavens and a new earth
f.r: Isaiah 66:22; 2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:1; Articles of Faith 1:10; D&C 101:25

n: Be glad and rejoice forever in what God creates: He will make Jerusalem a joy and her people a delight.
God Himself will rejoice in Jerusalem, and weeping and crying will never be heard there again.

f.w: the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her

n: No more infant deaths or lives cut short; someone who dies at a hundred will be considered young. D&C 101 explains that in the Millennium people will live to the “age of a tree” and then be changed in the twinkling of an eye.

f.w: the child shall die an hundred years old

f.g: A baby who lives only a few days.

n: People will build houses and live in them, plant vineyards and eat their fruit—enjoying the results of their own work.

f.w: they shall build houses, and inhabit them

n: No one will lose their home or harvest to invaders. God’s people will live long like trees and enjoy what their hands have made.

f.w: as the days of a tree

n: Their work won’t be wasted and their children won’t be born into disaster, because they and their children are blessed by the Lord.

f.w: They shall not labour in vain

n: Before they even call, God will answer; while they’re still speaking, He will hear. Perfect closeness between God and His people.

f.w: before they call, I will answer

n: Wolf and lamb will graze together, the lion will eat straw like an ox, and the serpent will eat dust. Nothing will hurt or destroy on God’s holy mountain—a picture of millennial peace that echoes Isaiah 11.

f.w: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together
dust shall be the serpent's meat
